scope: Three pinned original ECC integration test modules read whole and syntax parsed; no execution or fixture substitution.

findings.detail: Header/adaptive tamper tests compare repaired files byte-for-byte through check_eq_files, stronger than numeric success alone. ECC recovery tests also compare full output DB to backup.

Header repair injects five bytes at offset four in a single JPEG. Adaptive repair additionally injects offset1100 and last-five-byte changes. These finite cases do not establish all formats, boundary lengths, insertion/deletion or interrupted-source behavior.
Both header entry_assemble and adaptive stream_entry_assemble tests explicitly TODO multiple-block assembly; each expected assembly list has a single result.

Adaptive stream_entry_assemble expected ECC bytes include next entry marker and file2 metadata from dummy database. Test therefore does not enforce entry-local read containment. Actual production parser needs separate review before classifying exploitability or runtime corruption.

repair test_check explicitly omits index equality assertion because changing comments shifts offsets. Other repair tests validate selected index/marker corruption against known backup but not arbitrary index/body inconsistency.

repair tests rely on module setup generating header/adaptive DBs and backups from original fixture corpus. Importing or individually calling selected methods without setup would not be valid integration qualification.
